newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Nov coffee exports seen nearing Oct. levels.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Nov coffee exports seen nearing Oct. levels.

text.p: Brazilian coffee exports in the month of November could end up a lot nearer to the record overseas sales seen in October than earlier expected, exporter association officials said.
"If November exports don't reach October's level, I think they will be very near," said Jorge Esteve, president of the Brazilian Coffee Exporters Association (Abecafe).

"I would say we are going to ship a total of three million bags in November and December although I would not like to say how that will be divided between the two months," said Oswaldo Aranha, president of the Brazilian Coffee Exporters Federation.

According to the daily bulletin from the Rio de Janeiro Coffee Center, exports based on bills of lading by November 11 were 314,043 bags, virtually unchanged from the 329,874 bags loaded by the same stage in October.
Based on certificates of origin issued, figures were lower, covering 512,991 bags against 610,610 bags by the same period the previous month.

Final shipments in October amounted to 1.89 million bags, the highest monthly shipments since September 1993. The record exports were attributed mainly to sales carried over from September after a delay in lifting a state export tax.
"What we are seeing in November are left-overs from October when I actually thought we were going to ship over two million tonnes," Aranha said.
The October shipments brought total Brazilian exports since July to 5.79 million bags.
Under an agreement with other coffee producing nations, Brazil shoud ship no more than nine million bags in July to December 1996.
"I think we will be very slightly short of nine million bags but we will not go over," Aranha said.
In the next six month-period, January to June 1997, Brazil's quota is six million bags and despite the lower limit, there are already concerns about availability given internal demand.

One additional source of supply is monthly government stock auctions which in theory can go up to 200,000 bags but which so far have been for much smaller quantities, with the largest in the latest series for 85,466 bags to be held on November 20.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
